name: Dieu De Pagoda
kicker: National pagoda on the Gia Hoi river
summary: One of three Nguyễn national pagodas still standing in Hue, on the Hộ Thành river near Gia Hội bridge, built up in 1844 on the former garden of the future Emperor Thiệu Trị. Step through the river gate to the hall and its bronze censer. Go for a royal pagoda in the city itself, not out on the tomb road.
getThere: 100B Bạch Đằng, Phú Cát ward, near Gia Hội bridge.
heroCaption: The gate of Dieu De from the river

notice.title: No published fee or hours
notice.body: No ticket price or opening hours are published for Diệu Đế. Ask at the gate.

body: Diệu Đế stands on the Hộ Thành river, which Hue also calls the Gia Hội or Đông Ba river, at 100B Bạch Đằng, Phú Cát ward, near Gia Hội bridge. It is one of three Nguyễn national pagodas still standing in Hue.

Work began in the third month of Thiệu Trị 4, 1844, on the garden of Phúc Quốc Công, the future Emperor Thiệu Trị. An English page of the city site gives 1807 and a 5,000 square metre platform instead.
Walk across toward Gia Hội bridge and along Bạch Đằng to the gate.

figures.caption: The hall and the censer at Dieu De
figures.alt: A bronze censer in front of the hall at Dieu De Pagoda

gettingThere: From the south bank, cross toward Gia Hội bridge and follow Bạch Đằng to number 100B, Phú Cát ward.

legs.heading: From the south bank

admissionNote: Check on arrival. The city page prints no fee.
